warnings_strict_justification: AMReX builds with an extensive warning set and treats warnings as errors in CI (-Werror, -Wall, -Wextra, -Woverloaded-virtual, -Wnon-virtual-dtor and more in Tools/CMake/AMReXFlagsTargets.cmake), and runs clang-tidy with the modernize-* and deprecated-declarations checks.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: AMReX runs GitHub CodeQL over both its C++ and Python code on every push and pull request to development, and on a weekly schedule. CodeQL is configured with the security-and-quality query suite (.github/workflows/codeql.yml), which includes CodeQL's security queries for C/C++. These target common vulnerability classes mapped to CWE identifiers, including out-of-bounds reads and writes, use-after-free, integer overflow, uncontrolled format strings and unsafe library calls. Results are reported as GitHub code-scanning alerts and triaged by the maintainers. The project additionally undergoes periodic Coverity Scan analysis, and builds with clang-tidy and -Werror across GCC, Clang and Intel compilers in CI.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: AMReX is written in C++. Its CTest suite is run routinely in CI — on every pull request and push — against assertion-enabled debug builds across GCC, Clang, Intel, macOS and Windows. Assertions (AMREX_ASSERT, AMREX_ALWAYS_ASSERT) are compiled in by default in debug builds and enabled explicitly via AMReX_ASSERTIONS=ON, and AMReX_BOUND_CHECK adds bounds checking on Array4 array access. The build systems additionally support AddressSanitizer, UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer and ThreadSanitizer builds (FSANITIZER=TRUE, THREAD_SANITIZER=TRUE), which developers use when investigating memory-safety defects.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: AMReX processes only simulation inputs supplied by the user running it; it has no untrusted input boundary.

SECURITY.md documents the response process: reports go to the technical committee, are acknowledged within a few business days, assessed for affected versions and severity, fixed via development, and disclosed through a GitHub security advisory that credits the reporter.

build_standard_variables_justification: The CMake build system honors CC, CXX, CFLAGS, CXXFLAGS and LDFLAGS and extends rather than replaces them.
build_preserve_debug_justification: It can be done with CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE.
build_non_recursive_justification: AMReX does not use recursive builds in its CMake build system.
build_repeatable_justification: The AMReX library build is deterministic: rebuilding the same source with the same compiler and configuration produces identical output. No timestamps or build-host identifiers are embedded in the library.
installation_standard_variables_justific: AMReX's CMake installation honors the standard CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX and DESTDIR conventions, including in its custom install steps.
installation_development_quick_justifica: A developer gets the full source, build and test environment with the standard CMake convention: cmake -S . -B build -DAMReX_ENABLE_TESTS=ON && cmake --build build && ctest --test-dir build.
external_dependencies_justification:
External dependencies are declared in a computer-processable form by the CMake build via find_package (MPI, OpenMP, HDF5, HYPRE, PETSc, SUNDIALS, Conduit, Ascent, Catalyst, FFTW3, CUDAToolkit, rocFFT and others), and in the Spack and conda-forge package recipes.
https://amrex-codes.github.io/amrex/docs_html/BuildingAMReX.html
dependency_monitoring_justification: AMReX bundles no convenience copies of external code; its optional dependencies (MPI, HDF5, HYPRE, PETSc, SUNDIALS and others) are resolved from the system or from Spack/conda at build time, and Dependabot monitors the dependencies AMReX does control (its GitHub Actions) weekly.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: AMReX bundles no forked or convenience copies of external libraries; every optional dependency is located at build time with CMake find_package and supplied by the system or by Spack/conda, so updating a component is entirely independent of AMReX.

automated_integration_testing_justificat: GitHub Actions builds AMReX and runs its CTest suite on every pull request and push across GCC, Clang, Intel, CUDA, HIP, macOS and Windows, reporting pass/fail per job.

assurance_case_justification:
AMReX's assurance case is in SECURITY.md:
https://github.com/AMReX-Codes/amrex/blob/development/SECURITY.md#security-assurance-case

- Threat model: "Scope and threat model" — AMReX is a library with no network surface, no daemon, no credentials, and no privilege boundary; its inputs come from the same user who runs the job. The realistic threats are supply chain, memory-safety defects, and downstream misuse.
- Trust boundaries: "Trust boundaries" — a table of every interface (application code, inputs files, plotfile/checkpoint I/O, MPI, GPU kernels), none of which crosses a privilege boundary; the boundary that matters is development and distribution (repository, CI, release artifacts).
- Secure design principles: "Secure design principles" — least privilege, small attack surface, economy of mechanism (no vendored forks of dependencies), and supply-chain defense via reviewed PRs, CI on every PR, and Dependabot.
- Common implementation weaknesses: "Countering common implementation weaknesses" — explains why the OWASP Top 10 is largely inapplicable, and lists the countermeasures for the memory-safety and undefined-behavior CWE classes that do apply (CodeQL, clang-tidy, -Werror, ASan/UBSan/TSan builds, assertions, AMReX_BOUND_CHECK, multi-compiler/multi-GPU CI, Coverity).
